claim: present entries are work-RAM addresses 0x0000F9C3 + 26*k (26-byte parameter blocks); absent entries are 0xFFFFFFFF
why: In 12 of the present entries the value is off that grid: parts 23 and 24 of the six records 0xFD238F, 0xFD240F, 0xFD248F, 0xFD250F, 0xFD258F and 0xFD260F hold 0x0000FD6F and 0x0000FD89. (0xFD6F-0xF9C3) mod 26 = 4, and the two values are 26 apart. The text dates from 2026-09-02 in v10 (0599ad2c). This lane ported it to v9 (61c723da, line 2775) and to v7 (:2334) without re-checking the claim. Reproduce with verify_findings.py.
fix: present entries are 0xF9C3 + 26*k (part blocks, k = 0..23), except parts 23/24 of the six records 0xFD238F-0xFD260F, which point to 0xFD6F / 0xFD89 (a second pair of 26-byte blocks); absent = 0xFFFFFFFF. Fix all of v10:2775, v9:2775 and v7:2334.

claim: (written as <table> - <its length> because the dispatchers have no labels of their own in audio/audio_control_engine.s)
why: The labels already exist in the tree this lane was merged into: lane audio merged first, and `git show 6c16aad8:v10/maincpu/audio/audio_control_engine.s` has MidiStream_RecType48_SysExDispatch. In the frozen ELF, MidiStream_RecType48_SysExDispatch = 0xFCC9CB, RecType60_CtrlDispatch = 0xFCCA0D and RecType98_CmdDispatch = 0xFCCA45, equal to table entries 0x48/0x60/0x98. v9 has the same text.
fix: `.long MidiStream_RecType48_SysExDispatch` / `_RecType60_CtrlDispatch` / `_RecType98_CmdDispatch` (v10 and v9), and drop the parenthetical.

claim: D = 0x40 here where the other level tables hold 0x7F
why: The reader MidiCC_RxCC94_Celeste (0xFD0012) ends in `calr 0xfd036b` = MidiCC_Helper_ConditionalESetup, exactly like CC64 Sustain: E = D when the value is >= 0x40, else 0. The records are {part, 0x04, 0x40}, the same selector form as CC64's {part, 0x04, 0x08}, not the {0x05, part, 0x7F} form of the level tables. So D is an on-value/bit (0x40, beside sustain's 0x08), not a level maximum. The header does not mention the switch tail.
fix: 'records {u8 part, u8 0x04, u8 0x40}, same selector form as CC64; reader ends in MidiCC_Helper_ConditionalESetup, so E = 0x40 when value >= 0x40 else 0 (an on/off flag, cf. CC64's 0x08)'.

claim: 616 bytes each = 22 rows x 28 bytes, row-major, MSB = leftmost pixel ... at y=80
why: Draw_FlashMemUpdate_message_bitmap (0xEF5040) sets IX = DE+1 and does `dec 1, IX` at each new row: row 0 is drawn at y = DE and later rows go upward. So the bitmaps are stored bottom-up, and 'at y=80' is the bottom row. The PNG beside the .bin (v10/maincpu/images/Bitmap_1bit_Please_Wait.png) renders upside down, which confirms it.
fix: '22 rows x 28 bytes, stored BOTTOM-UP: the reader draws row 0 at y = DE and each later row one line higher (`dec 1, ix`); MSB = leftmost'. The y values are the bottom row. Flip the PNG round trip in mono_images.py.

The same dangling reference sits on FlashRead_BlockHandler_Table, FlashWrite_BlockRef_Type6 and the others. The file header (lines 1-8) still says 'Flash memory sector write routines'.

label_or_addr: DrawMonoBitmap header (0xFAFB48); same text in v9:8266, v7:8359
claim: the call is queued as a 20-byte DrawQueue_Alloc record ... and executed later by DisplayCmd_DequeueAndExecute
why: DrawMonoBitmap_DeferredPath calls DisplayCmd_DequeueAndExecute (0xFAA36C) right after filling the record, so that routine is the poster, not the executor. It runs TaskSched_WaitForEvent(3), then DisplayCmd_Execute_Type2 (0xFAA3EB). Type2 stores XWA into the ring at 0x03247C (`ld (XDE+IX),XWA; minc4 0x7c,IX`) and signals; the routine yields and retries while the ring is full. The record is run by the draw task in DrawTask_FuncDispatch (0xFAA311: `ld XHL,(XIZ); ld XWA,XIZ; call T,XHL`). uimisc's drawing_primitives.s header names that executor correctly.
fix: '... and posted to the draw-task ring at 0x03247C by DisplayCmd_DequeueAndExecute (an enqueue that retries while the ring is full, despite its name); the draw task later runs it through DrawTask_FuncDispatch (`ld xhl,(xiz); ld xwa,xiz; call (xhl)`)'. Apply to v9 and v7, and to the DrawLineWithMode/Dotted headers, which say 'as in DrawMonoBitmap'.

claim: 1 sets or clears bit 5 (_Impl_Mode1) and 2 bit 6 (_Impl_Mode2) according to the pixel's bit 7 -- the axis-aligned paths and the general path use OPPOSITE polarity (set-if-bit7 vs clear-if-bit7)
why: This is true only for mode 1. Mode 1: _Impl_Loop7/Loop8 do `bit 7,(xde); jr z; set 5` (set-if-bit7), and Loop9/Loop10 do `bit 7,(xix); jr z; res 5` (clear-if-bit7). Mode 2: all four paths, Loop11, Loop12, Loop13 and Loop14, do `bit 7; jr z; res 6` then `set 6`, i.e. clear-if-bit7 everywhere.
fix: '... according to the pixel's bit 7. In mode 1 the axis-aligned paths (_Loop7/_Loop8) set bit 5 when bit 7 is set and the general paths (_Loop9/_Loop10) clear it -- opposite polarity, as the ROM has it. In mode 2 all four paths clear bit 6 when bit 7 is set and set it otherwise.'

claim: skip when the entry equals 0xFDEDEF, else `call (xhl)`
why: All four readers compare with 0xFDECEF: 0xFDDE4D, 0xFDDECD, 0xFDDF7C and 0xFDDFFA each do `f2 ef ec fd 30  lda XWA,0xfdecef; cp XWA,XBC; ret Z`. 0xFDECEF is AudioInit_MixFallbackDefault_0x5, and no v10 entry of the table equals it, so the skip never fires with the shipped table. In v7 the value is 0xFDE509.

claim: Two 20-byte permutations of 0..0x13 (the SetWall slot numbers)
why: ROM bytes, row 0: 00 02 00 0a 03 04 05 06 0b 08 09 01 13 0c 0d 0e 0f 07 11 12 -- 0x00 appears twice and 0x10 is missing. Row 1: 02 0b 01 04 05 06 07 11 09 0a 03 08 0d 0e 0f 10 10 12 13 0c -- 0x10 appears twice and 0x00 is missing. Neither row is a permutation.
fix: 'Two 20-byte slot-number maps over 0..0x13, each one entry short of a permutation (row 0 repeats 0x00 and omits 0x10; row 1 repeats 0x10 and omits 0x00).' Rename to NoRef_SetWall_SlotMap20x2.

claim: the slot's byte +0 then gets back its own old high nibble (and 0xF0), so only the template's low nibble of byte +0 survives
why: Voice_InitSlotTemplate (0xF7210D), unidasm: 85 21 ld A,(XIY) / 95 11 ldirw / c9 cc f0 and A,0xf0 / b5 41 ld (XIY),A. The whole byte +0 is overwritten with (old & 0xF0), so its low nibble becomes 0 and nothing of template byte +0 survives (it happens to be 0x00 anyway). Same text in v9/v7.
fix: ; ...ldirw; then byte +0 is overwritten with its own old value AND 0xF0 (old high nibble kept, low nibble cleared), so template byte +0 is discarded.

claim: FAT12 when that record's word +36 (its highest cluster number) is 0xFFF
why: The volume-mount code (smf_event_processor.s:6480-6491, SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Helper6) computes the cluster count into word +54, then stores 0xFFFF into +36 when +54 > 4087 (and when partition type +4 >= 4, line 6215), else the 0xFFF default. So +36 is the FAT entry mask / end-of-chain value (0xFFF or 0xFFFF), and the highest cluster count lives at +54. The 'failed fetch returns (+36)-8' is therefore 0xFF7/0xFFF7, the FAT bad-cluster code. Lead F of the lane report repeats the error ('volume +36 highest cluster'). Same text in v9 (:4707) and v7 (:4695).
fix: ; FAT12 when the volume's word +36 (FAT entry mask / EOC value: 0xFFF for FAT12, 0xFFFF for FAT16, set at mount from the cluster count in +54 > 4087) is 0xFFF ... A failed fetch returns (volume +36) - 8 = 0xFF7/0xFFF7, the FAT 'bad cluster' code.

why: VoiceChannel_SelectPrevParam (0xF25F8C, source lines just below the table) never loads the table: `cp a,0 / jr z / dec 1,a / stb_dri`. `command grep -n -a VoiceChannel_ParamLimitTable` finds the real readers: VoiceSynth_HandleDataEntry, VoiceChannel_SelectNextParam, VoiceParam_HandleDataEntry, VoiceSynth_Algo_ChannelConfig, VoiceParam_ReadUpdate_6.
fix: ; Read by VoiceSynth_HandleDataEntry, VoiceChannel_SelectNextParam, VoiceParam_HandleDataEntry, VoiceSynth_Algo_ChannelConfig and VoiceParam_ReadUpdate_6 as `ld xiy, ... / ld E,(XIY+IX)`; SelectPrevParam does not use it (it floors at 0).

The reader is the unlabelled routine at 0xEF61E9, called from 0xEF607F: call SeqState_HasModeChanged / ld e,(0x0d65) / and e,3 / sla de,2 / ld xhl, table / ld XIY,(XHL+IY) / call T,XIY. Table and target names (DefaultHandler_Ret_DispatchTbl_Target0..3) inherit the wrong owner.

claim: Byte data, 6 B.  Read by ClockConfig_Handler_0 (0xEFA7BE)
why: ClockConfig_Handler_0 is 6 bytes: `anddi8 (0xe3e2),253 / ret`. The readers (lines 7313, 7350) are in ScoopParam_ValueTable_Sub_Helper (0xEFA7C9), a real routine entry that scoop_data_headers.routine_of skipped because its name matches the STRUCT regex `_Helper`. claim: Byte data, 4 B.  Read by VoiceSlot_StatusRet (0xEFC7B2) ... indexed with stride 4 (`sla hl, 2`), index from `ld a, (3429:16)`
why: The reader (line 11036, in the unlabelled routine called at 0xEFD05C, about 2 KB after VoiceSlot_StatusRet) is `ld a,(3429:16) / ld xhl, VoiceSlot_StatusRet_Tbl / ld_rr8b a, xhl, a / stb_d8 (0x0def), a`. That is a byte table, stride 1, 4 entries for display mode 0..3, giving the pop-up id (0,5,5,15) stored to 0x0DEF. The `sla hl, 2` belongs to the dispatch through VoiceSlot_StatusRet_DispatchTbl that follows. Same in v7 (:11188).

claim: Read by SoundEvt_LongPacketHandler (0xEF609D)
why: SoundEvt_LongPacketHandler is `ld (3923),0 / ordi8 / ld w,2 / call SoundEvt_LongPacketHandler_0x11 / ret`. The table is read by the routine it calls, at 0xEF60AE (unlabelled in the file; positional alias SoundEvt_LongPacketHandler_0x11): ld l,(3429) / and l,3 / sla hl,2 / ld xix, table. This is one of 45 such mis-citations in v10 (39 in v7) listed in reader_cite_v10_refined.txt.
fix: Label 0xEF60AE in the file and cite it: '; Read by <label> (0xEF60AE, called by SoundEvt_LongPacketHandler)'.

why: Scoop_CallDisplayHelper only loads XIY=Scoop_DisplayData_ButtonLayout and XIX=Scoop_DisplayData_ButtonLayout_0x8 (0xF00AAB). The reader of this list is the routine at 0xF00AAB, the XIX continuation handed to UIRender_TwoTableGeneral: ld xiy, Scoop_CallDisplayHelper_DisplayList / ld xix, ..._0x21 / call UIRender_TwoTableGeneral.

claim: Byte data, 80 B.  Read by PerfMode_VolumeParam_Process ... index from `ld l, (3424:16)`
why: Commit c32b63b4 spells the object as 20 .long RAM pointers (0xF9B9 + 0x1A*k), and the v10 header says '20 x u32 work-RAM pointers'. The reader computes the index as byte[0xF1A0 + (3424)-1] (`ld xix,0xf1a0 / ld_rrb l,xix,hl / sla hl,2`), i.e. through the part map, not from (3424) directly.

label_or_addr: AccChannel_StoreStateIfChanged (v10 0xF538EC; v9 same line; v7 wording is correct)
claim: (Like the routine above, the `and w` masks are applied to W, not to the A that is stored.)
why: In the routine above, AccChannel_StoreCurrentState (0xF538D5), A is masked: `c9 cc 7f` and A,0x7F, then `c8 cc 07` and W,7. It stores 0x32F7 & 0x7F. The new routine has both masks on W (0xF5391F `c8 cc 7f`, 0xF53922 `c8 cc 07`), so it stores 0x32F7 unmasked. The two routines behave differently.
fix: (Both `and` masks act on W, so 0x32F7 is stored unmasked. AccChannel_StoreCurrentState above masks A with 0x7F; only its `and 7` hits W.)

claim: Readers: SMF_Event_ProgramChange (0xF28999) and SMF_Event_ControlChange (0xF28A2D), identically: after checking the value is 0..0xF, ld xde, SMF_PartAssignTable / ldb_sri ...
why: The ControlChange copy of the lookup (0xF28A69-0xF28AB4: `bit 0,(0x10EB)` / `ld xde, SMF_PartAssignTable` / the SMF_CtrlChg_SearchPart loop) is dead code. It comes right after the unconditional `jr SMF_CtrlChg_UseDefault` at 0xF28A67 (`68 50`). range_refs.py v10 F28A69 F28A96 finds only the block's own loop branches (jr@F28A94, jr@F28AB2): no jr/jrl/calr or abs24 from outside. v7 0xF28A3F behaves the same: its one abs24 hit, at 0xFB3E6D, is operand bytes of `cp (0x8c9c),0x8a`. Only ProgramChange reads the table live.
fix: Reader: SMF_Event_ProgramChange (0xF28999): after checking the value is 0..0xF, `ld xde, SMF_PartAssignTable` / `ldb_sri A, ...`, then search 0xF1A0[0..15] (0x7F if none). SMF_Event_ControlChange holds an identical lookup at 0xF28A69, but it is unreachable: it follows `jr SMF_CtrlChg_UseDefault` and nothing branches into it. Also add a NO CALLER FOUND note on that block.

claim: "BOUND" records: every handler first reads the byte at the RAM address in u16 +2, ANDs it with u8 +4 and shifts it right by (u8 +5 & 0x0f), and draws according to that value.
why: bound[0x06] (0xFB2201) is the target of the lane's own SeGfx_BoundOp06. It and bound[0x0A] (0xFB2438) read a 16-bit WORD at RAM[u16 +2] (`94 04 pushw (XIX)` / `92 04 pushw (XDE)`) and never read +4 or +5. They format it with Sprintf_Locked (0xFF0A72), using "%1d"/"%2d"/"%3d" (0xEAB160.., 0xEAB1A8..) selected by u8 +9 (op 06) or u8 +0B (op 0A). The cell is u16 +7 and the style u8 +6. bound[0x01] is the null `ret` at 0xFB1589. The mask/shift prologue holds only for ops 00 02 03 04 05 07 08 09 0B.
fix: "BOUND" records: ops 00 02 03 04 05 07 08 09 0B first compute value = (RAM byte[u16 +2] & u8 +4) >> (u8 +5 & 15). Ops 06 and 0A instead print the 16-bit word at RAM[u16 +2] (no mask or shift) at cell u16 +7, style u8 +6, format %1d/%2d/%3d chosen by u8 +9 (06) or u8 +0B (0A). Op 01 is a null handler.

label_or_addr: 34 `; data-as-code (v10_data_as_code_census.py ...)` comments inside SeScreenData..SeScreenData_End (v10 only), e.g. :10588 above SeBitmap_EnvCurve1, :14236 above SeScreenData_0x39BE, :11891 above SeBitmap_Picture40x40

why: The comment gate carried these into the rendered block, where they now contradict the lane's own typing. 0xF10D1F-0xF10D2F is inside SeBitmap_EnvCurve1 (0xF10CAE-0xF10D75), which IS read (SeEnvCurve_BitmapTable entries 3 and 6, drawn by op 03), and the comment sits above that label instead of at its range. 0xF145C6-0xF14602 sits above a record-pointer table with named readers (SeMenu_PresetInit_TableLookup2, SeMenu_FilterEdit_Dispatch). The SeScreenData blocks in v9 and v7 carry 0 of them.
fix: Delete the 34 census comments between SeScreenData: and SeScreenData_End: in v10 (as v9/v7 already are). Optionally add one block-header line: "the 2026-09 data-as-code census flagged 34 spans here; all are typed screen data now". Then re-run the census.

claim: Single-record wrappers take the record in XIY, or -- the *_FromBuf ones and SeGfx_StaticOp03_BlitAtCell -- use the RAM record buffer at 0x0006CA that the caller has just filled
why: SeGfx_StaticOp03_BlitAtCell fills the buffer itself, from registers: `ld (1740),xiy` (+2 bitmap u32), `ld (1744),ix` (+6 cell), `ld (1746),bc` (+8 bytes per row), `ld (1748),hl` (+10 rows). Its XIY is a bitmap pointer, not a record. The SeEnvCurve reader calls it with XIY=bitmap, IX=cell, BC=5, HL=40.
fix: ...the *_FromBuf ones use the RAM record buffer at 0x0006CA that the caller has filled. SeGfx_StaticOp03_BlitAtCell builds the op-03 record there itself, from XIY = 1-bpp bitmap, IX = cell, BC = bytes per row, HL = rows.

claim: 7 LE32 pointers to the 40x40 envelope-curve bitmaps in SeScreenData, indexed 0..6
why: The reader (SeMenu_ShowConfirmDialog_Data_0x4A9, v10 0xF0F433, called from 0xF0F40A) computes the index as bits 7-5 of a RAM byte (`and a,0xe0 / srl 5,a`), so 0..7. Value 3 branches away (`cp a,3 / jr nz ..._Skip5`) and draws a framed box with ops 1B/00, so entry [3] (a second SeBitmap_EnvCurve1) is never read here. Value 7 is not range-checked and would read past the table, into SeMenu_WaveformSelect_End. The '0..6' range is not established by any code.
fix: 7 LE32 pointers indexed by bits 7-5 of the curve-type byte. Value 3 draws a framed box instead (ops 1B + 00), so entry 3 (a duplicate of EnvCurve1) is unread by this reader. Value 7 is not range-checked.

label_or_addr: string-table headers 'value range up to N' (10 of 24 tables, e.g. SeScreenData_0x21F2, 0x20C9, 0x213C, 0x21D4, 0x21E0, 0x259F, 0x2C32, 0x3A52, 0x3A5B)
claim: string table, 3-char cells, indexed by a bound record's value (field +7 of a bound op 02/07 record; value range up to 128)
why: N is the mask bound of the reading record (1 + mask>>shift), not what the table holds. SeScreenData_0x21F2 holds 14 3-char cells (42 B, " --".." +6") yet says 'up to 128'. SeScreenData_0x2C32 holds 3 bytes of 1-char cells yet says 'up to 4'. A reader would take the table as 128 or 4 entries long.
fix: Say both numbers: 'value = (RAM[ram] & mask) >> shift, at most N by mask; the table holds K cells' (K = extent / width). Where K < N, add 'values >= K would read past it'.

claim: 94 bytes after East_ClassTable_163 that no registration or code reference reaches. Contents not established. (UNKNOWN in the lane report)

claim: TimeSig_DisplayStrings (v10/v9 0xf65909, v7 0xf65505): `ld xde,<this>; add xde,xbc; ld xhl,(xde); call (xhl)`
why: 0xf65909 is ASCII time-signature text ('(1/2)+0  ' ...), not code.
